paragraphs.text: Pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma syndrome-8 is an autosomal dominant tumor predisposition with incomplete penetrance. It is characterized mainly by adrenal pheochromocytoma, which is often bilateral and usually benign. Qin et al. (2010) found that the mean age at diagnosis was similar to that of sporadic cases. Armaiz-Pena et al. (2021) concluded that patients with TMEM127 variants often resemble those with sporadic nonmetastatic pheochromocytoma. Paraganglioma and renal cell carcinoma may also occur, although these authors stated that the causal link needs further evaluation.

paragraphs.text: Yao et al. (2010) studied 20 TMEM127 mutation carriers from 20 independent families. All had adrenal tumors. Seven had bilateral tumors (P = 2.7 x 10(-4)), and 5 of the 20 had familial disease (P =.005). Median age at onset was 41.5 years in carriers and 45 years in patients without a mutation, a difference that was not significant (P =.54). The most common presentation was a single benign adrenal tumor in a patient older than 40 years. Malignancy occurred in 1 carrier (5%). Yao et al. (2010) concluded that germline TMEM127 mutations were associated with pheochromocytoma but not paraganglioma. They noted that these mutations occurred in an age group often excluded from genetic screening algorithms.

paragraphs.text: Toledo et al. (2015) offered clinical and genetic screening to 151 individuals from a six-generation family carrying a germline TMEM127 mutation. Clinical data were available for 34 mutation carriers, who were followed for 8.7 +/- 8.1 years. Of these, 11 (32%) were diagnosed with pheochromocytoma at a median age of 43 years. In 9 patients, symptoms began at 29 years (range, 10-55 years); 2 patients were asymptomatic. Tumors were multicentric in 5 patients (45%) and bilateral in 5 (45%). Six patients (54%) had at least one adrenomedullary nodule smaller than 10 mm. No paragangliomas, distant metastases, or other manifestations were found.

paragraphs.text: Stütz et al. (2020) reported a 61-year-old woman with a 4 x 4 x 6 cm paraganglioma in the left supraclavicular fossa. The tumor showed MIBG uptake and was positive for synaptophysin and chromogranin on histology; plasma free metanephrines were normal. She also had acromegaly due to a 13-mm GH-secreting pituitary macroadenoma. She had paroxysmal hypertensive crises, which the authors attributed to the acromegaly, and a multinodular goiter. Her family history was unremarkable. Surgery cured both tumors, and she remained well after 10 years of follow-up. She carried a TMEM127 variant of uncertain significance (see MOLECULAR GENETICS).

Overall, 4 TMEM127 variants were found among 12 families without mutations in other susceptibility genes (about 30% of familial cases), and 3 among apparently sporadic cases (about 3%). All mutations were germline, and none were present in 1,064 ethnically matched control alleles. Six of the 7 variants were splice site or nonsense (truncating) mutations. The mutations included a 1-bp insertion, a nonsense mutation, a 4-bp deletion, a second splice site mutation, and a missense mutation.

paragraphs.text: Qin et al. (2010) examined LOH at the TMEM127 locus in 35 pheochromocytomas. All 19 TMEM127-mutant tumors tested showed LOH with loss of the wild-type allele, compared with 2 of 16 wild-type tumors, consistent with a 2-hit tumor suppressor mechanism. TMEM127 expression was 4-fold lower in mutant tumors, which the authors suggested reflected instability of the mutant transcript. In HEK293 cells transfected with mutant TMEM127 constructs (M158 and M99), no protein product was detectable despite equivalent transfection efficiency, supporting a loss-of-function effect. On expression profiling, TMEM127-mutant pheochromocytomas clustered with NF1- and RET-mutant tumors and were enriched for kinase receptor signaling transcripts rather than hypoxia transcripts. TMEM127-mutant tumors showed increased S6K phosphorylation compared with normal adrenal medulla and TMEM127 wild-type tumors.
